interactions.summary: Jiang closes the previous point by insisting that blaming God for one's low station insults God, because the soul's position is self-chosen rather than divinely imposed.
A student reads Dante's lines in which Beatrice says free will is God's greatest gift, a vow binds human consent to God's consent, and compensation cannot simply reclaim what was already offered.

Jiang glosses the reading by saying free will is the chief sign of divine love, then interprets Piccarda's vow as a marriage of wills whose breaking counts not as a minor procedural lapse but as betrayal of God itself.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang interpretation with question back to class

claims.claim: Jiang says it insults God to imagine that God forced a soul into spiritual smallness, because the lower position is chosen rather than imposed.
The Dante passage being read presents free will as God's greatest gift and as the highest-value thing a human can pledge in a vow.
Jiang interprets the passage to mean that God gives Piccarda free will and Piccarda gives that same free will back to God, creating an inseparable bond rather than a revisable contract.
On Jiang's reading, once that vow-bound union exists, compensatory good acts cannot undo the break because violating the vow is equivalent to betraying God.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compresses the whole vow theology into a marriage metaphor: God gives free will, Piccarda hands it back, and what results is an eternal union that cannot be casually dissolved.
signature_moments.source_phrase: now they are eternally married right? If they're eternally married, you can't divorce
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's strongest memory-hook for why vow-breaking becomes far more than a technical failure.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes the moral charge maximal by saying Piccarda did not merely fail to keep a promise but betrayed God.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the severity of Jiang's reading and sets up the next round of class resistance.

glossary_terms.term: free will as God's greatest gift
glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The quoted and glossed premise that divine love is shown by granting creatures freedom rather than mechanical obedience.
Jiang's interpretive shorthand for a vow as the irreversible joining of human free will to God's consent.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet grounds Jiang's free-will reading directly in the Dante text and escalates the moral diagnosis from weak follow-through to outright betrayal of God through a broken vow.
